title: Why ionic crystals fracture
statement:
Why can an ionic crystal be brittle when layers are forced to slide?

[_]{a}

choices: The shift brings like charges together.
Neutral atoms all become free radicals.
Ionic bonds gain electrons from the applied pressure.
explanations: Breaking the crystal does not require changing ion identities.
Metallic bonding is a different model.
Pressure does not by itself add electrons.

hints: Moving a layer can align like charges.
solution: The lattice contains alternating charges. Moving a layer can align like charges. Repulsion can split the crystal. Electrostatic repulsion favors fracture.
